title: Unemployment Benefit Claims: Sequencing and Mutual Exclusion of Programs
content:
Programs of Unemployment Benefit Claims are sequenced and mutually exclusive across a claimant's claims. The following points state the governing rule and how each is read against the claim records.

## The rule

1. An Extended Benefits (EB) claim extends a Regular State Unemployment Insurance, UCFE, UCX or Combined Wage Claim record named on it as its parent claim, and a Trade Readjustment Allowances (TRA) claim extends the same kind of parent.
2. An Extended Benefits or Trade Readjustment Allowances claim may be determined monetarily eligible only when the claim named on it as its parent claim has status exhausted.
3. When an Extended Benefits claim also exists on the same parent, Trade Readjustment Allowances are paid only for weeks after that Extended Benefits claim is exhausted or closed.
4. A Disaster Unemployment Assistance (DUA) claim may be filed only when the claimant holds no Regular State Unemployment Insurance, UCFE, UCX or Combined Wage Claim record whose status is filed, active, on hold or inactive, because a claimant eligible for regular unemployment compensation is not eligible for disaster assistance.
5. Any one week ending date is paid under at most one claim: a weekly payment may be issued only when the count of payments standing for that week ending date across all of the claimant's claims is zero. That count is the number of weekly payments and reissued payments issued for that week ending date on any of the claimant's claims, less the number of those payments that have been cancelled.
6. A supplemental payment for a week already paid on the same claim, and a reissue of a cancelled payment, are not second weekly payments.

## How each point is read

**Parent status (point 2).** The status read is that of the parent claim named on the Extended Benefits or Trade Readjustment Allowances claim, as the claim records show it before the determination. Only status exhausted satisfies the point.

**Disaster filing (point 4).** The records read are all of the claimant's claims under the four regular programs; an exhausted, closed, withdrawn or ineligible regular claim is not among the statuses that block.

**One claim per week (point 5).** The count is taken across every claim the claimant holds, for the one week ending date to be paid.

| Payments standing for the week ending date across the claimant's claims | Weekly payment for that week ending date |
|---|---|
| None (no weekly payment or reissue, or every such payment cancelled) | May be issued |
| One weekly payment or reissue not cancelled, on any claim | Not issued |

### Hypothetical illustration

A claimant's UCFE claim was paid a weekly payment for the week ending on a given Saturday, and that payment was later cancelled; the count for that Saturday is one payment less one cancellation, that is zero, so a weekly payment for that week ending date is not barred by point 5.
